submission.name: Study Sprout
submission.tagline: Keep a little study buddy growing as your group works through its weekly tasks.
submission.inspiration: Our team wanted to make recurring study tasks feel less like a plain checklist, especially for students working together in a small course group. A small character seemed like a fun way to show progress without adding another complicated study planner.
submission.what_it_does: Students can add study tasks, mark them complete, and earn coins that help a plant-like companion grow. The app also shows a shared group progress view; the shop is a simple version with a limited set of decorations.
submission.how_we_built_it: We built a browser interface with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, plus a FastAPI backend in Python that stores task and companion data in JSON. The frontend sends updates through the API and refreshes the group view after changes.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: Combining separate frontend pieces and settling on a consistent data shape took time. The app works through the main flow, but rapid updates from multiple students can sometimes leave the displayed group totals stale until a refresh.
submission.accomplishments: We made the task-to-reward loop work from the browser through the backend, and drew the companion art ourselves. We are proud that the basic group view and character state survive a page reload.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned to agree on API shapes earlier and to keep features modular enough to change. We also saw how quickly a small shared-state feature can expose timing issues in a web app.
submission.whats_next: We would add more companion variations and a better decoration shop. We would also improve live updates and try a course platform connection if an appropriate API is available.
